text.zh: 1918年11月11日停战后的第二天，莫奈写信给总理克列孟梭，把睡莲作为和平的象征献给法国。
text.en: The day after the Armistice of 11 November 1918, Monet wrote to the prime minister, Georges Clemenceau, offering the Water Lilies to France as a symbol of peace.

text.zh: 莫奈亲自设计了这两个椭圆形展厅，画沿着弧形的墙面一圈排开。
text.en: Monet himself designed these two oval rooms, with the paintings following their curved walls.

text.zh: 他说，他想给观众“一个无边无际的整体、一片没有地平线也没有岸的波浪”的错觉。
text.en: He wanted to give viewers “the illusion of an endless whole, of a wave without horizon and without shore”.

text.zh: 8幅画，每幅高约2米，加起来总长超过91米。
text.en: Eight compositions, each about two metres high, stretch over 91 metres in total.

text.zh: 光从磨砂玻璃天花板上洒下来，天气和时间不同，画也会跟着变。
text.en: Light falls from a frosted glass ceiling, so the paintings change with the weather and the time of day.

text.zh: 橘园建于1852年，原本是给杜乐丽花园里的橙树过冬的温室。
text.en: The Orangerie was built in 1852 to shelter the orange trees of the Tuileries Garden in winter.

exclusive._说明: 独家发现“找回的光”：在“1960年代”（天花板被盖住，展厅变暗，只有人工灯光）和“今天”（自然光从磨砂玻璃天花板洒下）之间切换。这是示意，不是当年的真实样子。打开就算发现了卡片“自然光”。

note.zh: 20世纪60年代的翻修挡住了自然光，2006年才重新找回莫奈想要的光。这是示意。
note.en: Renovations in the 1960s blocked the natural light. In 2006, the light Monet wanted was restored. This is an illustration.

alt.en: Claude Monet, Water Lilies, Musée de l'Orangerie

title.zh: 第一幕 · 三十年的睡莲

text.zh: 从19世纪90年代末到1926年去世，莫奈用了将近三十年画他吉维尼花园里的睡莲池。这组巨大的画，是整个系列的顶峰。
text.en: From the late 1890s until his death in 1926, Monet spent nearly thirty years painting the water-lily pond in his garden at Giverny. These huge paintings are the summit of that cycle.

alt.en: Claude Monet, Water Lilies, Musée de l'Orangerie

title.zh: 第二幕 · 停战后的第二天

text.zh: 1918年11月12日，第一次世界大战停战后的第二天，莫奈写信给克列孟梭，要把这些画作为和平的象征献给国家。
text.en: On 12 November 1918, the day after the Armistice ended the First World War, Monet wrote to Clemenceau, offering these paintings to the nation as a symbol of peace.

alt.en: Claude Monet, Water Lilies, Musée de l'Orangerie

text.zh: 1927年，莫奈去世几个月后，展厅按他的设计开放。20世纪60年代的翻修挡住了自然光，直到2006年，展厅才恢复了莫奈想要的样子。
text.en: In 1927, a few months after Monet's death, the rooms opened according to his design. Renovations in the 1960s blocked out the natural light; only in 2006 were the rooms restored as Monet intended.

final.zh: 一片没有地平线也没有岸的波浪。
final.en: A wave without horizon and without shore.
